routing_warnings.description: The observed failure concerns accessibility of the shared link, not production of the video artifact.
The client changes the permitted video-delivery channel.
The replacement-link message concerns link-based delivery and does not explicitly claim completion of the video artifact.
The feedback enumerates narrower performance, script, and setting requirements rather than a failure of artifact production itself.
The message establishes the independently measurable duration constraint.
Posting another link is delivery evidence and is not a target-specific implementation claim for artifact production.
The reported defect concerns failure to follow the script.
The request to follow the script more closely concerns spoken-script fidelity, not whether the video is in Arabic MSA.
The reported failure is non-adherence to the script rather than a failure to use Arabic MSA.
The instruction to say every phrase exactly as written modifies the script-fidelity Requirement.
The freelancer disputes script adherence and the client's ability to assess the translation; it does not establish a change or execution result for Arabic MSA localization.
The report that the link does not work is execution evidence about link accessibility rather than delivery-channel selection.
The claim that anyone with the link can view the file concerns shared-link accessibility rather than delivery-channel selection.
This message changes the permitted delivery channel rather than independently establishing that a shared link is accessible.
The client requests direct chat delivery, which changes the delivery channel rather than shared-link accessibility.
Providing another link after the direct-chat request concerns compliance with the designated delivery channel; the message does not establish whether the link is accessible.
